I will keep it simple and grow the crops I know best: winter wheat and summer maize in the same fields. In Quzhou County, that is the safest way for me to make use of the whole year. I am 57, and with only primary schooling, I do not want to gamble on crops that need more market judgment or more complicated field management. Wheat and maize fit my land, my experience, and the local water conditions. Wheat gives me a steady harvest in early summer, and after that I can sow maize right away and get another crop from the same land.

For management, I will aim for steady production, not the highest possible input. I will use improved or hybrid seed because it is easier for me to get stable emergence and yield. I will prepare land with rotary tillage because it is practical and cheaper than deep ploughing every time. For fertilizer, I will use moderate nitrogen and balanced phosphorus and potassium so the crop does not grow too weak or lodge. I will irrigate wheat more times than maize because wheat in my area depends more on timely watering, especially at jointing and grain filling. I will spray pesticides only when needed, but I know wheat usually needs more disease and aphid control, while maize usually needs fewer applications if the stand is good. My goal is stable yield, manageable labor, and lower risk through the normal wheat-maize rotation.
